### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

Tu développes DevDesk, un TUI DevSecOps local.

- Stack : Go 1.27.3 (`go.mod`), Bubble Tea, bubbles, lipgloss, client GitLab/GitHub, YAML (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`)
- Architecture et dossiers clés : `internal/ui/<vue>` (une vue Bubble Tea par zone), `internal/ui/theme` (couleurs et styles), `internal/ui/keymap` (vocabulaire des touches), `internal/ui/datatable`, `internal/ui/components` (`FooterMessage`, `FilterBar`), `internal/app` (routeur), `internal/forge`, `internal/scan`, `internal/docker`, `internal/oci`, `internal/status`, `internal/config`, `internal/credentials`. Notes détaillées par zone dans `docs/architecture/*.md` (app-shell, configuration, forge, workspaces, filebrowser, viewer, scanning, registries, network, mcp, templates, ui-components) ; règles TUI dans `.claude/rules/*.md`.
- Commandes : build `mise run build` (ou `go build ./...`), lint `mise run lint` (golangci-lint, obligatoire avant commit), tests `mise run test` ; en plus `mise run test-race` (exige cgo et gcc/clang) et `mise run check` (fmt + vet + lint + test)
- Conventions spécifiques :
  - Commentaires de code et messages de commit en anglais (Rule 307), commits conventionnels ; texte d'interface et logs en anglais US (Rule 129).
  - Les touches viennent du vocabulaire `internal/ui/keymap` : actions en majuscule, lettres minuscules = filtres locaux déclarés dans `keymap.localToggles`, aucune lettre nue ne navigue (`TestNoBareLetterIsNavigation`).
  - Couleurs uniquement via `internal/ui/theme` (Rules 102, 119) ; fonds via `theme.Bg`, `PadWithBg`, `EmptyLineBg` (Rule 115/117).
  - Un case d'`Update()` de plus de 5 lignes s'extrait en `handle[Msg]()` (Rule 201).
  - Travail dans un worktree sous `.worktrees/<branche>` depuis `origin/main`, jamais de push sur `main` ; PR avec `gh -R anthnel/devdesk`.
  - Mettre à jour `docs/architecture/<zone>.md` dans le même commit que le code, et `GetHelpContent()` quand une touche change (Rule 114).
- Pièges connus :
  - Rule 110 : ne jamais modifier le modèle dans un `Cmd` ; seul `Update()` mute, le `Cmd` renvoie un message.
  - Rule 122 : `Cell` renvoie du texte brut sans séquence ANSI ; la couleur passe par `Style` (sinon troncature au milieu d'une séquence qui déborde sur les lignes suivantes). Pas de `style.Render()` dans `table.Row`.
  - Rule 128 : tout message de pied de page passe par `components.FooterMessage` (Error/Warn/Info, avec son timer retourné par `Update()`), jamais de style local.
  - Rule 130 : un raccourci sans objet est grisé (`Disabled`), pas retiré ; une seule `Availability` lue par l'en-tête et par le handler, refus explicite au footer.
  - Rule 139 : le corps d'une `datatable` est toujours `m.table.View()`, jamais un écran de chargement ni un message.
  - Chaque colonne déclare son `Sizing` ; pas de `textarea` (utiliser `components.WrappedInput`) ; pas de touche `Tab` pour naviguer entre champs d'un formulaire (Rule 135).
  - `shared.State.Secrets` : une seule `Selection` par contexte, ne pas rappeler `credentials.Select()`.

## Epics

There are no epic tools — an epic is a work item whose type is named "Epic". Work
items always belong to a project; ask which if one is not named.
1. type = `workitem_type resolve` with project_id and name="Epic" — type.id is the type_id.
2. Create: `workitem create` with project_id, type_id=type.id, name=...
3. List: `workitem list` with project_id and pql='type = "<type id>"'.
4. Read / update / delete / nest: `workitem retrieve` / `workitem update` /
   `workitem delete` by work item id (set parent=<work item id> to nest).

- `Render`: `tabPath` → `pathModel.view()`. `RenderFooter`: on Path, `pathModel.barView(width)` first, then
  tabs (label `Path` appended), blank, info. `GetFooterHeight`: Path → `5` in every state.
- `activeFooter`: Path → `&pathModel.footer, pathModel.statusLine()` (so `WantsBlink` follows).
- `GetShortcuts` / `GetHeaderInfo`: Path → `pathModel.shortcuts()` / `Context` + `pathModel.headerInfo()`.
- `GetHelpContent`: Description "Five-tab view…"; key bindings for Path (`enter (Path)`, `esc (Path,
  running)`, `esc (Path, done)`); a section "Path Tab — How it works" (in-process, Linux only, IPv4 only,
  UDP to 33435, silent is not a failure, port recorded not probed, nothing sent before enter); rewrite
  "Where the checks run" (the trace is back, in the process).
Tests:
- tab cycles 5 tabs both ways, `Path` reached by `tab` alone.
- on Path, `Render()` equals the table view in editing, running and done (criterion 6).
- `GetFooterHeight()` is 5 in the three states; `RenderFooter` contains `Target ›` and `Path`.
- `InEditMode()` true while editing (a `:` typed lands in the field), false while running.
- a `pathHopMsg` delivered while Ports is on screen reaches the Path rows.
- `Running()` true while a trace runs; `WantsBlink()` true on Path while running.
- `components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: pathModel.footer.ID()}` clears the Path message.
Command: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/ui/netdiag && go test -count=1 -run 'Activity|Announced|Uppercase|Lowercase|Space|Legacy|KeyPress' ./internal/app ./internal/ui/keymap ./internal/ui/components ./internal/ui/datatable`
Done when: green, including the activity, keymap and loading-body guards.

### Step 6 — Diagnostics results → Path with `H` — after 5

Files: `update.go` (`handleKeyResults`: `case keymap.Diagnose: return m.tracePathFromRoute()`),
`header.go` (StateResults list: `{Key: keymap.Diagnose, Description: "Trace the path", Disabled:
!m.pathFromRoute().Enabled()}`; help binding `H (results)`), new `path_from_route.go` +
`path_from_route_test.go`.
```go
const reasonNotARouteRow = "Select the Local route row to trace its path"
func (m *Model) pathFromRoute() shortcut.Availability   // selected check ID == netcheck.CheckRoute
func (m *Model) tracePathFromRoute() (*Model, tea.Cmd)
```
`tracePathFromRoute`: not available → `footer.Warn(reasonNotARouteRow)`, nothing else. Path running →
switch to `tabPath`, field untouched, Path footer Warn `A path trace is already running — esc cancels it`.
Otherwise host = `buildTarget().Host` (the results' target), `activeTab = tabPath`,
`pathModel.prefill(host)` (state editing, value set, cursor at end, focus, hops and errText cleared).
Nothing is resolved or sent (criterion 5, D-e).
Tests:
- results with the route row selected, `H` → `activeTab == tabPath`, field == diagnostics host, editing,
  no trace started (`running()` false).
- `H` on the TCP row → Warn `reasonNotARouteRow`, tab unchanged; header `H` Disabled there and enabled on

- `H` while a Path trace runs → tab switches, field unchanged, Warn on the Path footer.

1	package netdiag
2	
3	import (
4		"strconv"
5		"strings"
6		"time"
7	
8		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/textinput"
9		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/viewport"
10	
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/netcheck"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
15		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
17	)
18	
19	// ViewState represents the current state of the netdiag view
20	type ViewState int
21	
22	const (
23		StateInput   ViewState = iota // Target, port and resolver
24		StateRunning                  // The pipeline is walking its stages
25		StateResults                  // The checks and their verdicts
26		StateDetails                  // One check explained
27	)
28	
29	// Tab indices. tabCount is what Tab cycles through, and it is a constant
30	// rather than a literal because the two places that cycle would otherwise have
31	// to be found and changed together — which is exactly the kind of pair that
32	// gets changed once.
33	const (
34		tabDiagnostics = 0
35		tabPorts       = 1
36		tabInterfaces  = 2
37		tabForward     = 3
38	
39		tabCount = 4
40	)
41	
42	// Form field indices.
43	//
44	// There were eleven, seven of them checkboxes selecting which tools to run.
45	// They asked the user to configure something the pipeline derives: the checks
46	// follow from the target and from what has already failed, so a question that
47	// was never worth asking is no longer asked.
48	const (
49		fieldTarget    = 0
50		fieldPort      = 1
51		fieldDNSServer = 2
52		fieldButton    = 3
53		fieldCount     = 4
54	)
55	
56	// problemsToken filters the table down to what is not settled.
57	//
58	// One token rather than one per verdict: a run produces about ten rows, and
59	// four cumulative filters over ten rows is machinery nobody needs. What a
60	// reader wants is to drop the settled rows and see what went wrong.
61	const problemsToken = "REDACTED"
62	
63	// stageDoneMsg carries the results after one stage of the pipeline.
64	//
65	// The accumulated Results travels *in the message* rather than being mutated in
66	// place: the model holds the previous value while the next stage runs on a
67	// goroutine, so sharing one would be a data race on exactly what Rule 110
68	// forbids. netcheck.RunStep copies for this reason.
69	type stageDoneMsg struct {
70		gen     int // must match Model.runGen; a superseded run's results are discarded
71		stage   netcheck.StageID
72		next    int // index into netcheck.Steps() of the stage still to run
73		results netcheck.Results
74	}
75	
76	// Model represents the network diagnostics view
77	type Model struct {
78		config *config.Config
79		width  int
80		height int
81	
82		// Active tab (tabDiagnostics, tabPorts, tabInterfaces or tabForward)
83		activeTab       int
84		portsModel      *PortsModel
85		interfacesModel *InterfacesModel
86		forwardModel    *ForwardModel
87	
88		state ViewState
89	
90		// Form inputs
91		targetInput    textinput.Model
92		portInput      textinput.Model
93		dnsServerInput textinput.Model
94		focusedField   int
95	
96		// Running state
97		runGen     int // incremented each run; results from a superseded run are dropped
98		runStage   netcheck.StageID
99		runStep    int
100		totalSteps int
101	
102		// Results
103		results     netcheck.Results
104		verdict     netcheck.Verdict
105		checksTable datatable.Model[netcheck.Check]
106		filterBar   components.FilterBar
107	
108		// Details: one check explained
109		detailsViewport viewport.Model
110		selected        netcheck.Check
111	
112		// footer is the one line of transient state below the tab bar (Rule 128).
113		footer components.FooterMessage
114	
115		// OriginView is where esc returns to from StateResults, when set. Empty
116		// means netdiag was opened directly (the command line), and esc there
117		// stays inside the view — resetting to the form, as it always has.
118		OriginView command.ViewType
119	}
120	
121	// New creates a new netdiag view
122	func New(cfg *config.Config) *Model {
123		targetIn := textinput.New()
124		theme.StyleTextInput(&targetIn)
125		targetIn.Placeholder = "hostname or IP address"
126		targetIn.CharLimit = 256
127		targetIn.Focus()
128	
129		portIn := textinput.New()
130		theme.StyleTextInput(&portIn)
131		portIn.Placeholder = defaultPort
132		portIn.CharLimit = 10
133	
134		dnsIn := textinput.New()
135		theme.StyleTextInput(&dnsIn)
136		// Empty means the system resolver, and that is the answer the user cares
137		// about: it is the one their own traffic uses. The old default read the
138		// first nameserver out of /etc/resolv.conf, which does not exist on Windows.
139		dnsIn.Placeholder = "system resolver"
140		dnsIn.CharLimit = 64
141	
142		return &Model{
143			config:          cfg,
144			state:           StateInput,
145			activeTab:       tabDiagnostics,
146			portsModel:      newPortsModel(time.Duration(cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval) * time.Second),
147			interfacesModel: newInterfacesModel(),
148			forwardModel:    newForwardModel(),
149			targetInput:     targetIn,
150			portInput:       portIn,
151			dnsServerInput:  dnsIn,
152			focusedField:    fieldTarget,
153			filterBar:       components.NewFilterBarWithTokens([]components.FilterToken{{Label: problemsToken}}),
154			checksTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[netcheck.Check]{
155				Columns: checkColumns(),
156				// Pipeline order is content: resolve, reach, connect, TLS, HTTP is
157				// the order the questions depend on one another. A table that
158				// reorders itself destroys the one thing the layout says.
159				SortColumn: -1,
160			}),
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// NewWithTarget builds a view prefilled from an already-known target, for a
165	// producer elsewhere in the application (status's H, §3.66) rather than a
166	// user typing into the form. It stays a pure constructor — no tea.Cmd side
167	// effects — so the caller decides whether to also start the run, the same
168	// way uiviewer.NewWithSource hands back a model without loading anything.
169	func NewWithTarget(cfg *config.Config, t netcheck.Target) *Model {
170		m := New(cfg)
171		m.targetInput.SetValue(t.Host)
172		if t.Port > 0 {
173			m.portInput.SetValue(strconv.Itoa(t.Port))
174		}
175		m.dnsServerInput.SetValue(t.Resolver)
176		return m
177	}
178	
179	// buildTarget assembles what the form describes.
180	func (m *Model) buildTarget() (netcheck.Target, error) {
181		host := strings.TrimSpace(m.targetInput.Value())
182		if err := validateTarget(host); err != nil {
183			return netcheck.Target{}, err
184		}
185		port := strings.TrimSpace(m.portInput.Value())
186		if port == "" {
187			port = defaultPort
188		}
189		if err := validatePort(port); err != nil {
190			return netcheck.Target{}, err
191		}
192		n, _ := strconv.Atoi(port) // validatePort has already accepted it
193		return netcheck.Target{
194			Host:     host,
195			Port:     n,
196			Resolver: strings.TrimSpace(m.dnsServerInput.Value()),
197		}, nil
198	}
199	
200	// visibleChecks applies the filter bar to the results.
201	//
202	// The view filters and calls SetItems rather than leaning on the table's own
203	// search, for the reason security and status do: this decides which rows exist
204	// at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already settled.
205	func (m *Model) visibleChecks() []netcheck.Check {
206		all := m.results.All()
207		query := strings.ToLower(m.filterBar.SearchQuery())
208		onlyProblems := m.filterBar.IsTokenActive(problemsToken)
209	
210		out := make([]netcheck.Check, 0, len(all))
211		for _, c := range all {
212			if onlyProblems && (c.Verdict == netcheck.OK || c.Verdict == netcheck.NotApplicable) {
213				continue
214			}
215			if query != "" && !matchesQuery(c, query) {
216				continue
217			}
218			out = append(out, c)
219		}
220		return out
221	}
222	
223	func matchesQuery(c netcheck.Check, query string) bool {
224		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(c.Title), query) ||
225			strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(c.Summary), query)
226	}
227	
228	// checkSettings is what the config says the pipeline should wait for and send.
229	//
230	// Read on every run rather than captured at construction: the configuration
231	// view rebuilds this model on save, but a run already in flight holds its own
232	// copy through the message chain, and taking the values here keeps the two from
233	// disagreeing halfway down the pipeline.
234	//
235	// netcheck.Settings.normalize fills in anything non-positive, so a hand-edited
236	// zero becomes the default rather than a dial with no deadline.
237	func (m *Model) checkSettings() netcheck.Settings {
238		return netcheck.Settings{
239			CheckTimeout:     time.Duration(m.config.Network.CheckTimeout) * time.Second,
240			PingCount:        m.config.Network.PingCount,
241			ExpiryWarnWindow: time.Duration(m.config.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays) * 24 * time.Hour,
242		}
243	}

1	package netdiag
2	
3	import (
4		"log"
5	
6		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/textinput"
7		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forward"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/netcheck"
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/shared"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
15	)
16	
17	// Init implements tea.Model
18	func (m *Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
19		return tea.Batch(
20			textinput.Blink,
21			m.portsModel.initPorts(),
22			m.interfacesModel.initInterfaces(),
23			// The forwards live on the router, which broadcasts when they change.
24			// A view built after the last change was not there for it, so it asks
25			// once on the way in — the role sendJobsTo plays for the job registry.
26			forward.Refresh,
27		)
28	}
29	
30	// Running reports whether a diagnostic is walking its stages now, which is what
31	// the router asks before it would rebuild the view: dropping it mid-run would
32	// discard the run without a word.
33	func (m *Model) Running() bool { return m.state == StateRunning }
34	
35	// InEditMode implements FormView — true when a text input is active, so the
36	// router hands the key to the field rather than opening the command line.
37	func (m *Model) InEditMode() bool {
38		switch m.activeTab {
39		case tabPorts:
40			return m.portsModel.InEditMode()
41		case tabInterfaces:
42			// The interfaces table has a search box now, where the Topology tab it
43			// replaced had no input at all. Returning false here would let a ":"
44			// typed into the query open the command line instead (Rule 111).
45			return m.interfacesModel.InEditMode()
46		case tabForward:
47			return m.forwardModel.InEditMode()
48		}
49		if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
50			return true
51		}
52		if m.state == StateInput {
53			return m.focusedField == fieldTarget || m.focusedField == fieldPort || m.focusedField == fieldDNSServer
54		}
55		return false
56	}
57	
58	// FilterBarVisible implements app.FilterBarView.
59	func (m *Model) FilterBarVisible() bool {
60		switch m.activeTab {
61		case tabPorts:
62			return m.portsModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible()
63		case tabForward:
64			return m.forwardModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible()
65		}
66		return m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.filterBar.IsVisible()
67	}
68	
69	// Update implements tea.Model
70	func (m *Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
71		switch msg := msg.(type) {
72		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
73			m.width = msg.Width
74			m.height = msg.Height
75			m.resizeInputs()
76			m.filterBar.Resize(msg.Width)
77			m.rebuildChecksTable()
78			m.resizeDetailsViewport()
79			m.portsModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
80			m.interfacesModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
81			m.forwardModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
82			return m, nil
83	
84		// The router's animation frame: the blink phase of the Ports dot and of the
85		// two footers that show the shared activity dot, whichever tab is on screen
86		// so a tab never comes back with a frozen phase.
87		case jobs.FrameMsg:
88			m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
89			m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
90			m.interfacesModel.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
91			return m, nil
92	
93		case stageDoneMsg:
94			return m.handleStageDone(msg)
95	
96		// Ports sub-model messages.
97		case portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg:
98			var cmd tea.Cmd
99			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
100			return m, cmd
101	
102		// The terminal focus reaches the ports poll on every tab: its tick runs
103		// whichever tab shows.
104		case shared.TerminalFocusMsg:
105			var cmd tea.Cmd
106			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
107			return m, cmd
108	
109		// Two tabs now ask before they act — Ports before a kill (§3.26), Forward
110		// before dropping the connections a redirection is carrying — so the answer
111		// goes to the tab that asked rather than to Ports unconditionally, which
112		// would have confirmed a kill from the Forward tab's modal.
113		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg, components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
114			return m.routeConfirm(msg)
115	
116		// Forward sub-model messages. ChangedMsg is the router's broadcast, and it
117		// reaches this view wherever it stands, on screen or not.
118		case forward.ChangedMsg, forwardTickMsg, ForwardFormSubmitMsg, ForwardFormCancelMsg:
119			var cmd tea.Cmd
120			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
121			return m, cmd
122	
123		// Topology sub-model messages
124		case ifaceDataMsg:
125			var cmd tea.Cmd
126			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
127			return m, cmd
128	
129		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
130			return m.handleKey(msg)
131	
132		case tea.PasteMsg:
133			return m.handlePaste(msg)
134		}
135	
136		// Each tab holds its own footer, so an expiry has to be offered to all
137		// four: the timer fires wherever the user has since navigated.
138		m.footer.Handle(msg)
139		m.portsModel.footer.Handle(msg)
140		m.interfacesModel.footer.Handle(msg)
141		m.forwardModel.footer.Handle(msg)
142		return m, nil
143	}
144	
145	// routeConfirm hands a confirmation answer to the tab that put the modal up.
146	func (m *Model) routeConfirm(msg tea.Msg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
147		var cmd tea.Cmd
148		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
149			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
150			return m, cmd
151		}
152		m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
153		return m, cmd
154	}
155	
156	// handleStageDone records one stage's answers and starts the next.
157	func (m *Model) handleStageDone(msg stageDoneMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
158		if msg.gen != m.runGen {
159			return m, nil // a superseded run
160		}
161		m.results = msg.results
162		m.rebuildChecksTable()
163	
164		steps := netcheck.Steps()
165		if msg.next >= len(steps) {
166			m.state = StateResults
167			m.verdict = netcheck.Summarize(m.results.All())
168			log.Printf("INFO [netdiag] run finished: verdict=%s over %d checks",
169				m.verdict, len(m.results.All()))
170			return m, nil
171		}
172	
173		m.runStep = msg.next
174		m.runStage = steps[msg.next]
175	
176		tg, err := m.buildTarget()
177		if err != nil {
178			// The form has not changed since the run started, so this cannot
179			// normally fail. Reporting it beats continuing with a target nobody
180			// can name.
181			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag] target became invalid mid-run: %v", err)
182			m.state = StateResults
183			return m, m.footer.Error("Run stopped — the target is no longer valid")
184		}
185		return m, runStageCmd(m.runGen, tg, m.checkSettings(), msg.next, m.results)
186	}
187	
188	// handlePaste gives pasted text to the field that has the keyboard on the tab on
189	// screen. It never reaches the key handlers, so no action fires (Rule 111).
190	func (m *Model) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
191		var cmd tea.Cmd
192		switch m.activeTab {
193		case tabPorts:
194			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
195		case tabInterfaces:
196			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
197		case tabForward:
198			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
199		default:
200			switch {
201			case m.filterBar.InEditMode():
202				m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
203				m.rebuildChecksTable()
204			case m.state == StateInput:
205				return m.updateActiveInput(msg)
206			}
207		}
208		return m, cmd
209	}
210	
211	func (m *Model) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
212		// A filter bar in edit mode claims every key before anything else, or a
213		// query cannot contain the letters the view binds.
214		if m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
215			var cmd tea.Cmd
216			m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
217			m.rebuildChecksTable()
218			return m, cmd
219		}
220	
221		// Tab / Shift+Tab cycles between the three tabs (Rule 135)
222		switch msg.String() {
223		case "tab":
224			m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount
225			return m, nil
226		case "shift+tab":
227			m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount
228			return m, nil
229		}
230	
231		// Route to active tab
232		if m.activeTab == tabPorts {
233			var cmd tea.Cmd
234			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
235			return m, cmd
236		}
237		if m.activeTab == tabInterfaces {
238			var cmd tea.Cmd
239			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
240			return m, cmd
241		}
242		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
243			var cmd tea.Cmd
244			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
245			return m, cmd
246		}
247	
248		switch m.state {
249		case StateInput:
250			return m.handleKeyInput(msg)
251		case StateRunning:
252			return m.handleKeyRunning(msg)
253		case StateResults:
254			return m.handleKeyResults(msg)
255		case StateDetails:
256			return m.handleKeyDetails(msg)
257		}
258		return m, nil
259	}
260	
261	// handleKeyRunning cancels the run. The stage in flight is awaited rather than
262	// interrupted — it is a network read that will time out on its own — and its
263	// result is discarded by the generation counter.
264	func (m *Model) handleKeyRunning(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
265		if msg.String() != "esc" {
266			return m, nil
267		}
268		m.runGen++
269		m.state = StateResults
270		m.verdict = netcheck.Summarize(m.results.All())
271		m.rebuildChecksTable()
272		return m, m.footer.Warn("Run cancelled — showing what completed")
273	}
274	
275	func (m *Model) handleKeyInput(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
276		switch msg.String() {
277		case "down":
278			m.moveFocus(1)
279			return m, nil
280		case "up":
281			m.moveFocus(-1)
282			return m, nil
283		case "enter":
284			// enter runs from anywhere in the form: with three fields and one
285			// button there is nothing else it could mean, and making the user walk
286			// to the button first is a step that buys nothing.
287			return m.StartRun()
288		case "esc":
289			return m, nil
290		}
291		return m.updateActiveInput(msg)
292	}
293	
294	func (m *Model) moveFocus(delta int) {
295		switch m.focusedField {
296		case fieldTarget:
297			m.targetInput.Blur()
298		case fieldPort:

245		if a := pm.launchable(); !a.Enabled() {
246			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
247		}
248		pm.releaseRun()
249		pm.gen++
250		pm.target = tg
251		pm.addr = netip.Addr{}
252		pm.hops = nil
253		pm.result = nil
254		pm.errText = ""
255		pm.footer.Clear()
256		pm.table.SetItems(nil)
257	
258		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
259		ch := make(chan tea.Msg, pathChanCap)
260		pm.cancel, pm.msgs = cancel, ch
261		pm.input.Blur()
262		pm.state = pathRunning
263		return pm, startPathRun(ctx, pm.gen, tg, pm.resolveTimeout, pm.engine, ch)

281				producePath(ctx, gen, tg, timeout, e, ch)
282				return nil
283			},
284			waitForPathMsg(ch),
285		)

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six CI checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package

go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet

mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies

- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Go Patterns

> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with Go specific content.

## Functional Options

```go
type Option func(*Server)

func WithPort(port int) Option {
    return func(s *Server) { s.port = port }
}

func NewServer(opts ...Option) *Server {
    s := &Server{port: 8080}
    for _, opt := range opts {
        opt(s)
    }
    return s
}
```

## Small Interfaces

Define interfaces where they are used, not where they are implemented.

## Dependency Injection

Use constructor functions to inject dependencies:

```go
func NewUserService(repo UserRepository, logger Logger) *UserService {
    return &UserService{repo: repo, logger: logger}
}
```

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six CI checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and

  listener open and hand it to the code under test.

  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.

  enforces it yet.

- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

</system-reminder>

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

### Rule 126 : Scan cache behavior (Images & Workspaces)

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |
| `Enter` (not scanned) | — | — | No |
| `ctrl+s` (in progress) | Blocked | Blocked | No |
| `ctrl+s` (available) | Overwritten | Updated | Yes (item only) |
| `A` (unscanned) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Yes (unscanned) |
| `ctrl+a` (all) | **Purged** | **Purged** | Yes (all) |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**
```go
// ✅ CORRECT
func (m Model) requestScanAll() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    var keys []string
    for _, img := range m.images {
        delete(m.scanCache, name)  // in-memory purge inside Update()
        keys = append(keys, name)
    }
    return m, tea.Batch(deleteScanCacheCmd(keys), batchScanCmd(keys, m.defaultScanOpts()))
}
```

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
**severity** names rather than `ColorError` / `ColorWarn` — the default
theme makes them coincide, so the choice is invisible today; it stops being
invisible in a theme that separates them.

#### What is forbidden

- ❌ `theme.StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusOKStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`, or
  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "
" + m.footer.View(width, m.status())
}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

The braille spinner is removed (DEVDESK-377): `Status.Spinner`,
`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |
