122	// verdictCell is plain text: the colour is decided by Style (Rule 122).
123	func verdictCell(c netcheck.Check) string {
124		switch c.Verdict {
125		case netcheck.OK:
126			return theme.IconOK + " OK"
127		case netcheck.Warn:
128			return theme.IconWarning + " WARN"
129		case netcheck.Fail:
130			return theme.IconError + " FAIL"
131		case netcheck.NotApplicable:
132			return theme.IconCanceled + " N/A"
133		default:
134			return theme.IconCanceled + " ?"
135		}
136	}
137	
138	// verdictStyle gives each verdict its own colour.
139	//
140	// Rule 122 reserves colour for what is worth spotting without reading, and its
141	// worked example — a container list where nearly every row is `running` —
142	// argues against colouring the nominal state. This column is the other case,
143	// and the difference is what the reader is doing: a diagnostic is read once,
144	// end to end, to find where it broke. Every row is a distinct question, there
145	// is no majority state to drown in, and the column *is* the answer. So the four
146	// outcomes are told apart at a glance, as Rule 121 has status indicators do.
147	//
148	// The one that is not a colour choice is UNKNOWN. It must not share N/A's dim:
149	// "no meaning here" and "we could not look" are the distinction the whole
150	// package is built on — the reason Verdict's zero value is Unknown and the
151	// reason SecretVerdict returns a *bool. Rendering them alike on screen would
152	// give back exactly what the types take care to keep apart.
153	func verdictStyle(c netcheck.Check) lipgloss.Style {
154		switch c.Verdict {
155		case netcheck.Fail:
156			return theme.SeverityTextStyle("CRITICAL")
157		case netcheck.Warn:
158			return theme.SeverityTextStyle("MEDIUM")
159		case netcheck.OK:
160			return theme.StatusOKStyle
161		case netcheck.Unknown:
162			return theme.SeverityTextStyle("HIGH")
163		default: // NotApplicable — nothing was asked, so nothing is worth spotting
164			return theme.DimStyle
165		}
166	}

168	// renderDetailsContent draws one check: what was observed, what it means, what
169	// to do, and the facts behind it.
170	func (m *Model) renderDetailsContent(width int) string {
171		c := m.selected
172		e := netcheck.Explain(c)
173	
174		var lines []string
175		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
176		lines = append(lines, section(width, "Observed", e.Observed)...)
177		lines = append(lines, section(width, "What it means", e.Means)...)
178		if e.Do != "" {
179			lines = append(lines, section(width, "What to do", e.Do)...)
180		}
181	
182		if len(c.Facts) > 0 {
183			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconConfig+" Details"), width))
184			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
185			for _, f := range c.Facts {
186				line := theme.KeyStyle.Render("  "+f.Key+" "+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + theme.Bg(f.Value)
187				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(line, width))
188			}
189			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
190		}
191	
192		if len(c.Phases) > 0 {
193			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconConfig+" Timing"), width))
194			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
195			lines = append(lines, phaseLines(c.Phases, c.Duration, width)...)
196			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
197		}
198	
199		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
200	}
201	
202	// phaseLabelWidth fits the longest phase name ("Connect"/"Content", 7
203	// characters) plus one cell of breathing room before the bar starts.
204	const phaseLabelWidth = 8
205	
206	// phaseLines renders one waterfall row per phase: a label, a bar proportional
207	// to the phase's share of total, and that share as a percentage. total is
208	// the check's own Duration — the phases already sum to it (see httpPhases),
209	// so the same value anchors both the bars and the numbers beside them.
210	func phaseLines(phases []netcheck.Phase, total time.Duration, width int) []string {
211		lines := make([]string, 0, len(phases))
212		for _, p := range phases {
213			var pct float64
214			if total > 0 {
215				pct = float64(p.Duration) / float64(total) * 100
216			}
217			fill := theme.GaugeFillWidth(pct, theme.TimingBarWidth)
218			bar := theme.TimingFillStyle().Render(theme.GaugeFill(fill)) +
219				theme.GaugeTrackStyle().Render(theme.GaugeTrack(theme.TimingBarWidth-fill))
220			label := theme.KeyStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("  %-*s", phaseLabelWidth, p.Name))
221			pctText := theme.Bg(fmt.Sprintf(" %3.0f%%", pct))
222			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(label+bar+pctText, width))
223		}
224		return lines
225	}
226	
227	// section renders a titled block of prose, wrapped to the pane.
228	func section(width int, title, body string) []string {
229		if strings.TrimSpace(body) == "" {
230			return nil
231		}
232		lines := []string{
233			theme.PadWithBg(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconConfig+" "+title), width),
234			theme.EmptyLineBg(width),
235		}
236		wrapped := lipgloss.NewStyle().Width(max(width-4, 20)).Render(body)
237		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(wrapped, "\n") {
238			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  "+line), width))
239		}
240		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
241		return lines
242	}

248	}

34	// GetShortcuts implements HeaderView
35	func (m *Model) GetShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
36		tabShortcuts := shortcut.Shortcuts{
37			{Key: "tab", Description: "Switch tab"},
38		}
39	
40		if m.activeTab == tabInterfaces {
41			// A read in flight greys the table's keys rather than removing them:
42			// the tab is the same screen either side of a refresh, and a column
43			// that empties and refills on every ctrl+r is the flicker Rule 130 is
44			// about. ctrl+r stays lit — asking again is exactly what still applies.
45			loading := m.interfacesModel.loading
46			return append(tabShortcuts, shortcut.Shortcuts{
47				{Key: "ctrl+r", Description: "Refresh"},
48				{Key: "/", Description: "Filter", Disabled: loading},
49				{Key: ".", Description: "Sort", Disabled: loading},
50				{Key: "?", Description: "Help"},
51			}...)
52		}
53	
54		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
55			if m.forwardModel.form != nil {
56				// A form is a mode, so the whole list is replaced rather than
57				// greyed (Rule 130): greying N and K here would show the union of
58				// two vocabularies.
59				return shortcut.Shortcuts{
60					// ←→ only cycles the type, so it greys elsewhere (Rule 130).
61					{Key: "←→", Description: "Change type", Disabled: !m.forwardModel.form.TypeFocused()},
62					{Key: "enter", Description: "Open the forward"},
63					{Key: "esc", Description: "Cancel"},
64				}
65			}
66			if m.forwardModel.table.FilterBar().InEditMode() {
67				return shortcut.Shortcuts{
68					{Key: "enter/esc", Description: "Confirm / Cancel search"},
69				}
70			}
71			return append(tabShortcuts, shortcut.Shortcuts{
72				{Key: keymap.New, Description: "New forward"},
73				// Nothing to pause, resume or delete on an empty table (Rule 130).
74				{Key: "space", Description: m.forwardModel.toggleLabel(), Disabled: !m.forwardModel.switchable().Enabled()},
75				{Key: keymap.Kill, Description: "Delete forward", Disabled: !m.forwardModel.closable().Enabled()},
76				{Key: "/", Description: "Search"},
77				{Key: ".", Description: "Sort"},
78				{Key: "?", Description: "Help"},
79			}...)
80		}
81	
82		if m.activeTab == tabPorts {
83			if m.portsModel.table.FilterBar().InEditMode() {
84				return shortcut.Shortcuts{
85					{Key: "enter/esc", Description: "Confirm / Cancel search"},
86				}
87			}
88			sc := shortcut.Shortcuts{
89				{Key: "t", Description: "Toggle TCP"},
90				{Key: "u", Description: "Toggle UDP"},
91				{Key: "l", Description: "Toggle LISTEN"},
92				{Key: "e", Description: "Toggle ESTAB"},
93				{Key: "n", Description: "Toggle numeric"},
94				{Key: "z", Description: "Reset filters"},
95				{Key: "/", Description: "Search"},
96				{Key: "space", Description: "Pause/Resume"},
97				// A socket the system declines to attribute carries no PID, so
98				// there is nothing to signal (Rule 130).
99				{Key: keymap.Kill, Description: "Kill process", Disabled: !m.portsModel.killable().Enabled()},
100				{Key: "?", Description: "Help"},
101			}
102			return append(tabShortcuts, sc...)
103		}
104	
105		switch m.state {
106		case StateInput:
107			return append(tabShortcuts, shortcut.Shortcuts{
108				{Key: "enter", Description: "Run the checks"},
109				{Key: "?", Description: "Help"},
110			}...)
111		case StateRunning:
112			return shortcut.Shortcuts{
113				{Key: "esc", Description: "Cancel and keep what completed"},
114			}
115		case StateResults:
116			if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
117				return shortcut.Shortcuts{
118					{Key: "enter/esc", Description: "Confirm / Cancel search"},
119				}
120			}
121			sc := shortcut.Shortcuts{
122				{Key: "enter", Description: "Explain the check"},
123			}
124			label := "Show problems only"
125			if m.filterBar.IsTokenActive(problemsToken) {
126				label = "Show every check"
127			}
128			escLabel := "New diagnostic"
129			if m.OriginView != "" {
130				escLabel = "Go back"
131			}
132			sc = append(sc,
133				shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "p", Description: label},
134				shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "/", Description: "Search"},
135				shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "ctrl+r", Description: "Run again"},
136				shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "esc", Description: escLabel},
137			)
138			if m.OriginView != "" {
139				// Otherwise esc already reads "New diagnostic" and does exactly
140				// this — advertising both here would just say the same thing
141				// twice (Rule 138). With an origin, esc means "go back" instead,
142				// so this is the only key left that starts a fresh target.
143				sc = append(sc, shortcut.Shortcut{Key: keymap.New, Description: "New diagnostic"})
144			}
145			sc = append(sc, shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "?", Description: "Help"})
146			return append(tabShortcuts, sc...)
147		case StateDetails:
148			return shortcut.Shortcuts{
149				{Key: "esc", Description: "Go back to the checks"},

155	// GetHeaderInfo implements HeaderView.
156	//
157	// The verdict is the one line worth spending: it is the answer to the question
158	// the view exists for, and reading it off ten rows is what the header is
159	// supposed to save. It appears only once there is a run to summarise.
160	func (m *Model) GetHeaderInfo(context string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
161		info := []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
162			{Key: "Context", Value: context, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
163		}
164		if m.activeTab == tabInterfaces {
165			return append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{
166				Key:   "Interfaces",
167				Value: m.interfacesModel.summaryLine(),
168				Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle,
169			})
170		}
171		if m.activeTab == tabPorts {
172			return append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{
173				Key:   "Ports",
174				Value: m.portsModel.summaryLine(),
175				Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle,
176			})
177		}
178		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
179			return append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{
180				Key:   "Forwards",
181				Value: m.forwardModel.summaryLine(),
182				Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle,
183			})
184		}
185		if m.activeTab != tabDiagnostics || m.state == StateInput {
186			return info
187		}
188		if len(m.results.All()) == 0 {
189			return info

229	// RenderFooter implements FooterView
230	func (m *Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
231		var parts []string
232	
233		// The active tab's filter bar renders above the tab bar when visible.
234		switch {
235		case m.activeTab == tabPorts && m.portsModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible():
236			parts = append(parts, m.portsModel.table.FilterBar().View())
237		case m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.filterBar.IsVisible():
238			parts = append(parts, m.filterBar.View())
239		case m.activeTab == tabInterfaces && m.interfacesModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible():
240			parts = append(parts, m.interfacesModel.table.FilterBar().View())
241		case m.activeTab == tabForward && m.forwardModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible():
242			parts = append(parts, m.forwardModel.table.FilterBar().View())
243		}
244	
245		tabs := theme.RenderTabs([]theme.TabItem{
246			{Label: "Diagnostics"},
247			{Label: "Ports"},
248			{Label: "Interfaces"},
249			{Label: "Forward"},
250		}, m.activeTab)
251		tabBar := theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg(" ")+tabs, width)
252	
253		// The message belongs to the tab that raised it: each sub-model keeps its
254		// own, so switching away does not carry one tab's notice onto another.
255		footer, status := m.activeFooter()
256		parts = append(parts, tabBar, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), footer.View(width, status))
257		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
258	}

274	// statusLine is what the diagnostics tab derives on every frame: a progress
275	// label while the pipeline walks, and nothing once it has an answer. It is a
276	// status rather than a footer message because it is a state, not an event —

122	// verdictCell is plain text: the colour is decided by Style (Rule 122).
123	func verdictCell(c netcheck.Check) string {
124		switch c.Verdict {
125		case netcheck.OK:
126			return theme.IconOK + " OK"
127		case netcheck.Warn:
128			return theme.IconWarning + " WARN"
129		case netcheck.Fail:
130			return theme.IconError + " FAIL"
131		case netcheck.NotApplicable:
132			return theme.IconCanceled + " N/A"
133		default:
134			return theme.IconCanceled + " ?"

138	// verdictStyle gives each verdict its own colour.
139	//
140	// Rule 122 reserves colour for what is worth spotting without reading, and its
141	// worked example — a container list where nearly every row is `running` —
142	// argues against colouring the nominal state. This column is the other case,
143	// and the difference is what the reader is doing: a diagnostic is read once,
144	// end to end, to find where it broke. Every row is a distinct question, there
145	// is no majority state to drown in, and the column *is* the answer. So the four
146	// outcomes are told apart at a glance, as Rule 121 has status indicators do.
147	//
148	// The one that is not a colour choice is UNKNOWN. It must not share N/A's dim:
149	// "no meaning here" and "we could not look" are the distinction the whole
150	// package is built on — the reason Verdict's zero value is Unknown and the
151	// reason SecretVerdict returns a *bool. Rendering them alike on screen would
152	// give back exactly what the types take care to keep apart.
153	func verdictStyle(c netcheck.Check) lipgloss.Style {
154		switch c.Verdict {
155		case netcheck.Fail:
156			return theme.SeverityTextStyle("CRITICAL")
157		case netcheck.Warn:
158			return theme.SeverityTextStyle("MEDIUM")
159		case netcheck.OK:
160			return theme.StatusOKStyle
161		case netcheck.Unknown:
162			return theme.SeverityTextStyle("HIGH")
163		default: // NotApplicable — nothing was asked, so nothing is worth spotting
164			return theme.DimStyle
165		}
166	}

168	// renderDetailsContent draws one check: what was observed, what it means, what
169	// to do, and the facts behind it.
170	func (m *Model) renderDetailsContent(width int) string {
171		c := m.selected
172		e := netcheck.Explain(c)
173	
174		var lines []string
175		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
176		lines = append(lines, section(width, "Observed", e.Observed)...)
177		lines = append(lines, section(width, "What it means", e.Means)...)
178		if e.Do != "" {
179			lines = append(lines, section(width, "What to do", e.Do)...)
180		}
181	
182		if len(c.Facts) > 0 {
183			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconConfig+" Details"), width))
184			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
185			for _, f := range c.Facts {
186				line := theme.KeyStyle.Render("  "+f.Key+" "+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + theme.Bg(f.Value)
187				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(line, width))
188			}
189			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
190		}
191	
192		if len(c.Phases) > 0 {
193			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconConfig+" Timing"), width))
194			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
195			lines = append(lines, phaseLines(c.Phases, c.Duration, width)...)
196			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
197		}
198	
199		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
200	}
201	
202	// phaseLabelWidth fits the longest phase name ("Connect"/"Content", 7
203	// characters) plus one cell of breathing room before the bar starts.
204	const phaseLabelWidth = 8
205	
206	// phaseLines renders one waterfall row per phase: a label, a bar proportional
207	// to the phase's share of total, and that share as a percentage. total is
208	// the check's own Duration — the phases already sum to it (see httpPhases),
209	// so the same value anchors both the bars and the numbers beside them.
210	func phaseLines(phases []netcheck.Phase, total time.Duration, width int) []string {
211		lines := make([]string, 0, len(phases))
212		for _, p := range phases {
213			var pct float64
214			if total > 0 {
215				pct = float64(p.Duration) / float64(total) * 100
216			}
217			fill := theme.GaugeFillWidth(pct, theme.TimingBarWidth)
218			bar := theme.TimingFillStyle().Render(theme.GaugeFill(fill)) +
219				theme.GaugeTrackStyle().Render(theme.GaugeTrack(theme.TimingBarWidth-fill))
220			label := theme.KeyStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("  %-*s", phaseLabelWidth, p.Name))
221			pctText := theme.Bg(fmt.Sprintf(" %3.0f%%", pct))
222			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(label+bar+pctText, width))
223		}
224		return lines
225	}

227	// section renders a titled block of prose, wrapped to the pane.
228	func section(width int, title, body string) []string {
229		if strings.TrimSpace(body) == "" {
230			return nil
231		}
232		lines := []string{
233			theme.PadWithBg(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconConfig+" "+title), width),
234			theme.EmptyLineBg(width),
235		}
236		wrapped := lipgloss.NewStyle().Width(max(width-4, 20)).Render(body)
237		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(wrapped, "\n") {
238			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  "+line), width))
239		}

- **App guard:** `TestActivityGuardScansThePathTabSources` and the rest of the app/keymap/components guards pass (run with `-run 'Activity|Footer|Announced|Uppercase|Lowercase|Space|Legacy|KeyPress|Netdiag|Guard'`).

  - `TestAgentUsageTrailSitsOnTheTopBorder`: the title line renders with `-` where the test expects a path.
  - `TestListContextsFailureReportsListOperation`: `listContexts()` returns `ContextListMsg`, not `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`.
  - `TestARetryFromAnotherViewClearsTheFailure` and `TestAFailureFromSecIsClearedByWorkspaces`: ws would not find the failure that `:sec` posed.
  - `TestAContextWithoutAListenAddressBindsTheDefault`: port 7777 is already in use on this machine.
- **`go test -count=1 ./internal/ui/...`:** fails only in `internal/ui/workspaces`, `TestJumpToPathSynthesizesDrillDownState`, which expects Unix-style `/tmp/...` paths.

**What changed (all under `internal/ui/netdiag/` unless noted)**
- **`model.go`:** `tabPath = 4`, `tabCount = 5`, and a `pathModel` field built with `systemPathEngine()`. `resolveTimeout` is `checkSettings().Normalized().CheckTimeout`.
- **`path_run.go`:** the `//nolint:unused` is gone.
- **`path_model.go`:** `update` now passes any message it doesn't handle to the input after `footer.Handle`, so `cursor.BlinkMsg` reaches the field.
- **`update.go`:** `Running()` also covers a running trace. `InEditMode`, paste, key, `WindowSizeMsg` and `jobs.FrameMsg` route to Path. The three Path messages (`pathResolvedMsg`, `pathHopMsg`, `pathDoneMsg`) route to it on any tab, and the fall-through goes through `pathModel.update`, so a hop arriving while another tab is on screen still lands.
- **`header.go`, `view.go`:**
  - **Path tab:** `Render`, `GetShortcuts`, `GetHeaderInfo`, `activeFooter` and the tab bar now include Path. The footer height constant is `pathFooterHeight = 5`, and `RenderFooter` puts the target bar first.
  - **Help text:** "Five-tab" description, the `enter (Path)`, `esc (Path, running)` and `esc (Path, done)` bindings, a new "Path Tab — How it works" section, and the rewritten "Where the checks run".
  - **Not changed:** `WantsBlink` in `ports_activity.go` already follows `activeFooter()`.
- **`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`:** `migratedSources[ViewNetdiag]` now includes `path_model.go`, `path_target.go` and `path_view.go`. I left `path_run.go` out, since it holds the I/O. I added `path_view.go` because it passed the activity guard and `footer_guard_test.go`, which only inspects `RenderFooter`/`InfoLine`/`InfoText` functions; `path_view.go` has none.

**Open points**
- `docs/architecture/network.md` is not updated yet (the code-and-docs-in-one-commit rule); I left it for the next step.
- I did not touch `activity_guard_test.go`'s comment above the netdiag entry; it doesn't mention `path_run.go`, which could be added.
- The Diagnostics inputs still don't receive `cursor.BlinkMsg`; that gap predates this change and is not part of this step.
